intro.text: A small spren who follows Venli everywhere, hidden in her sphere pouch, and wants to bond her. "Timbre" is Venli's nickname for her; her real name is unknown.
A spren who has bonded the singer Venli, something thought impossible, making her a Surgebinder. "Timbre" is Venli's nickname for her.
A Reacher spren bonded to the singer Venli, granting her the powers of a Willshaper. "Timbre" is Venli's nickname for her.

items.text: Timbre's grandfather was one of the spren who bonded Knights Radiant, and he was killed with thousands of others in the Recreance. Even so, late in the Era of Solitude, Timbre crossed into the Physical Realm to form a bond, choosing a singer rather than a human because of that example.
Shortly before the Everstorm, Timbre stayed close to Eshonai, who was in stormform at the time and found the little spren's presence annoying. Timbre would not give up.

Timbre stayed with Eshonai's body until a search party led by Ulim found it. Venli saw her while stripping off Eshonai's Shardplate and tried to shoo her away, but Timbre followed her, even as she took on envoyform. When Venli noticed her, she instinctively hid her from the Fused, fearing they would kill the little spren.

From then on Timbre went everywhere with Venli, riding in her sphere pouch and coming out only when no one could see. Venli, hostile at first, kept hiding her and gave her a nickname. Outside Kholinar, Timbre made clear she wanted to bond Venli, who doubted she could live up to Eshonai. Timbre began pulsing to the Rhythm of Peace to push back Odium's influence, and helped Venli hear the old rhythms again.

When Dalinar drew Venli into a highstorm vision, Timbre somehow followed and reached her as Odium tore the vision apart, before Dalinar sent them both out. At the Battle of Thaylen Field she stayed hidden in Venli's pouch, pulsing to Peace until she grew too frightened of Odium to continue.

After the battle, Venli slipped away and began to speak the First Ideal. When a Fused noticed and grabbed her pouch, Timbre used the confusion to leap into Venli's gemheart and trap the Voidspren living there. Once he had gone, Venli drank in Stormlight in a private cabin, proving Timbre had made her a Surgebinder.

Timbre told Venli about her grandfather and her distrust of humans, and urged her to tell the awakened parshmen the true story of the listeners. She warned Venli that travelling into Shadesmar would be dangerous. When their one attempt to shape stone drew secretspren, Timbre grew uneasy whenever Venli looked into Shadesmar.

As Venli resolved to lead her followers to freedom, Timbre urged her to let each of them choose for themselves rather than force her views on them. She was unhappy when Venli credited her powers to her Voidspren, and her reminder that their plans meant risk led Venli to check Shadesmar just in time to see Lady Leshwi approaching.

At a conclave of singers, Timbre reminded Venli that she would never be granted the Fused's immortality, and was frightened when the Nine sang an alien song together. When Leshwi lent Venli to Raboniel for the infiltration of Urithiru, Timbre was excited: in the tower they would be among Radiants who might help train her.

On the way to Urithiru, Timbre and Venli watched the Deepest Ones with curiosity, and were frightened when Raboniel noticed and revealed she knew Venli spied for Leshwi. When Raboniel explained the Surge of Cohesion, Timbre pulsed to Caution to hold back Venli's excitement.
When an ambush in the tunnels forced Venli to kill a human in self-defence, Timbre pulsed to the Rhythm of the Lost, but Venli refused her comfort.

Timbre was sure the Pursuer was mad, and protested when Venli compared Lezian to a spren, saying she did more than merely exist. She was pleased when Venli admitted she truly followed Timbre rather than her Voidspren, and pulsed to Hope as they silently rooted for the humans' desperate assault on the pillar room.

Timbre was amused when Venli told Raboniel she wanted to become Fused, doubting she had ever truly wanted that. Sensing Venli's doubts as she plotted with Dul, Timbre offered ideas to keep their group safe, and persuaded Venli to tell her how Axindweth had given her the gemstone holding Ulim.

Timbre was appalled that Raboniel had executed hidden Radiants, and anxious when Kaladin's family was held for the Pursuer. She blocked Venli's rhythms until they could talk privately and convinced her to act. Venli told Leshwi about the family, though not that she was Radiant, and slipped into an old rhythm she could hear only through Timbre, which encouraged the spren.

Watching over the unconscious Radiants, Timbre suggested that modern Radiants surprised the Fused because no ancient Radiants were limiting their training. She was excited to learn that secretspren were useless in the tower, and saddened when the Fused worked out where the tower's nodes might be.

Timbre hummed the Rhythm of the Lost with Venli when she met Rlain, and wanted her to show him she was Radiant, but Venli could not. When Venli stood up to Raboniel to claim Rlain, Timbre attuned Conceit to steady her, though the new rhythm hurt her. Venli then spoke words she thought would be her next Ideal, but they were not accepted, as Venli knew she had been hypocritical.
When Venli felt she was to blame for her people's suffering, Timbre reminded her that she had helped her resist Odium.

Practising Cohesion, Venli failed with Stormlight but spoke with the stones using Voidlight, and Timbre gleefully resonated with their tone. Three spren like Timbre then appeared: Reachers wanting to bond Venli's friends, like squires. Venli, fearing for them, had Timbre send them away until they could escape Urithiru.

As Venli and Rlain smuggled the tower's maps to the infirmary, Timbre told her these times called for dangerous choices, and that Ulim had manipulated her. The message of hope in the shash glyphs on the humans' foreheads resonated with her.

Encouraged by Timbre, Venli attuned a blend of Cultivation's and Odium's tones and shaped a small sculpture of the ancient listeners. When they learned Kaladin was dying, Timbre grew more and more excited until Venli proposed freeing Lift, the Edgedancer, from her cell.

Timbre was annoyed that Venli planned to hide her powers and pretend to have a Shardblade, but she fed the Rhythm of Hope into the rock to help Venli open a hole into the cell. When Venli asked if she could speak her Second Ideal now, Timbre told her she would know when the time was right.

Timbre warned Venli to lie when Raboniel asked if she hated herself, but Venli admitted she did. When Raboniel showed her a report of a large group of Parshendi on the Shattered Plains, Timbre prompted Venli to tell Rlain her whole story, and she did.

When Venli decided to leave with her people using Raboniel's writ, Timbre told her she was disappointed. Venli suggested she find a singer who cared more, but Timbre insisted she wanted Venli, her "wonderful mistake", and that Venli would do what was right.
With the Oathgates unusable, Timbre saw a chance to help the Radiants and kept pushing Venli to act, though Venli could see no real way to.

When the Pursuer's soldiers moved to kill the unconscious Radiants and Leshwi's troops stood aside, Timbre prompted Venli once more, and this time Venli drew in Stormlight and revealed their bond to Leshwi. Asked whether others like her wanted to bond singers, Timbre said there were some, but that Rlain was already spoken for.

Timbre rejoiced with Venli when she was reunited with her mother. When Venli told Thude she would help restore the bond between her people and the spren, her words were accepted, bringing their bond to the Second Ideal.

appearance.text: In the Physical Realm, Timbre looks like a ball of light trailing a comet-like white streak as she moves.

personality.text: Curious and adventurous, Timbre ventures into danger, yet she fears the Everstorm and hides in the shadows when it comes. She is determined in her pursuit of Venli and a calming influence on her, pulsing to the Rhythm of Peace to push Odium's influence away.
Timbre cannot speak. She communicates by pulsing to the rhythms, and Venli understands her pulses as words and intentions; Timbre, in turn, can read Venli's thoughts.
Disliking the idea of bonding humans again, she sought a singer. As Venli confronts her past, Timbre consoles and encourages her again and again, even when Venli refuses her comfort.
